From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 3, 2025 at 9:12 AM PST
Subject: Failover flag rollout + release gating (regional failover automation)

Connor,

Before we enable any portion of the automated regional failover path in production, I want us aligned on the rollout stages + release gates. This is the kind of change that can turn a bad day into a much worse day if we don’t have crisp stop/rollback criteria.

Can you confirm (or propose) a staged plan that Release Eng will enforce? I’m looking for something like:

1) OFF in prod (code deployed, flag hard off)
2) Monitor-only (evaluate triggers + emit decisions/audit events, but do not change routing/DNS)
3) Canary mitigation (automated action allowed only for a very small, low-risk slice; e.g., 1% of Hosted traffic OR a single internal route)
4) Progressive expansion (10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%), with explicit approvals at each step

Release gates I expect:
- Runbook updated and reviewed (SRE on-call can operate it, not just authors)
- Dashboards exist (region health + failover state machine + customer impact) and have a human-readable “what changed” view
- “Safe-to-failover” capacity checks wired up for target regions (no failover if headroom is below threshold)
- Clear rollback: disabling the flag must stop further automated actions, and we have a documented procedure to revert/neutralize any routing policy changes already applied

Also: I want the policy on who can approve “more than monitor-only” in prod. My default is:
- SRE on-call + Release Eng must be in the loop for each step
- Any step that could move >10% of traffic cross-region requires explicit go/no-go + an active comms plan

If you can send back a proposed checklist + sign-off matrix today, I’ll review and we can lock it this week.

Thanks,
Priya

—
Priya Natarajan
VP Engineering, Platform
Redwood Inference



From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 3, 2025 at 10:01 AM PST
Subject: Re: Failover flag rollout + release gating (regional failover automation)

Priya — agreed on the framing. Proposed staged rollout + gating below.

Rollout stages (prod):
A. Code deployed, flag OFF (default)
B. Monitor-only (flag ON, actions disabled; orchestrator posts state + would-have-taken-action events)
C. Action canary (flag ON, actions enabled ONLY for allowlisted scope)
   - scope is by route + customer tier (initially: a single low-risk Hosted route + internal canary account)
   - max cross-region traffic shift capped at 1%
D. Progressive failover enablement (expand cap: 5% -> 10% -> 25% -> 50% -> 100%)
   - each step is a change request with a specific start/end window

Release gates (must-haves before Stage B):
- Confluence runbook: “Automated region failover” marked READY and linked from on-call index
- Dashboards live: region health rollup, failover state transitions, and per-tier error/latency impact
- Alert rules exist but paging is tuned (burn-rate alerts are warning-only at B; paging allowed at C+)
- RBAC: override endpoints limited to SRE on-call + Release Eng (we have an internal ticket in flight to finalize groups)

Additional gates before Stage C (any automated action in prod):
- “Safe-to-failover” checks enabled (capacity headroom + dependency health gates)
- Explicit stop conditions encoded:
  - max shift cap (hard)
  - hold-down timer after action
  - abort if target region capacity drops below threshold mid-action
- Game day completed in staging with sign-off (SRE + Routing)

Approvals / sign-off matrix:
- Stage B (monitor-only): Release Eng (me) + SRE lead on rotation (Sean / delegate)
- Stage C (action canary <=1%): Release Eng + SRE on-call (acting IC) + Smart Routing EM (Mina or delegate)
- Stage D (>10% cap OR any scheduled production controlled failover window): add VP Infra & Reliability (Neha) approval and a comms checklist

Rollback expectations / procedure:
1) Immediate: disable action flag (stops new routing/DNS changes)
2) Revert: apply “baseline routing policy” preset in policy store (documented as a single command)
3) DNS/edge: if any DNS health-based records were changed, revert to prior target set; TTL strategy stays conservative during initial rollout
4) Verification: confirm region health dashboards stabilize + error budget burn returns to baseline within 10–15 min; note in #incidents with links

If you’re good with this, I’ll translate into a formal release checklist + a “Go/No-Go” template and tie it to ENG-2851 so it’s enforced as part of the change window.

Connor

—
Connor O’Brien
Release Engineering Lead
Redwood Inference



From: Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>, Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 3, 2025 at 11:18 AM PST
Subject: Re: Failover flag rollout + release gating (regional failover automation)

+1 overall.

Two SRE notes to bake into the gating doc:

1) Hold-down timers / flappiness:
   - For Stage C and beyond, we should require a minimum hold-down (e.g., 30 min) after any automated action before the trigger engine is allowed to take another action for the same region.
   - We should also require that the “recovery” threshold be materially different from the “degrade” threshold (hysteresis) so we don’t oscillate.

2) Ownership during the window:
   - If we’re enabling actions in prod (even canary), we should treat it like a controlled change with an acting IC + observer, not “just a flag flip.”
   - The IC must have clear authority to disable actions immediately if we see cross-region saturation or customer-visible regression.

If you want a simple rule: anything beyond monitor-only should happen only when SRE on-call is available to watch the dashboards for the full window.

Sean

—
Sean Gallagher
Director, Site Reliability Engineering
Redwood Inference



From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwoodinference.com>, Sean Gallagher <sean.gallagher@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, Mar 3, 2025 at 1:47 PM PST
Subject: Re: Failover flag rollout + release gating (regional failover automation)

Thanks both.

Connor — proceed with your proposed stages. Please incorporate Sean’s hold-down + IC/observer requirements explicitly (not implied) in the release checklist.

Two tweaks:
- Stage C: keep it strictly allowlisted *and* cap the action set (routing policy only, no DNS/edge changes) for the first canary. DNS/edge automation can come after we’ve seen at least one clean canary window.
- Stage D: for any step >10% cap, require a written go/no-go posted ahead of time (what we’re changing, why, expected customer symptoms, stop conditions, rollback).

Neha — FYI this matches what we discussed: monitor-only first, then small action canary with very tight guardrails.

Connor, please schedule a 30-min go/no-go review later this week (you + Sean + me; Neha optional depending on scope) before we move from Stage B to Stage C.

Priya

—
Priya Natarajan
VP Engineering, Platform
Redwood Inference
